content:
"Coming Out of the Ice" is a memoir written by Victor Herman, an American who was imprisoned in a Soviet labor camp in Siberia for more than a decade. The book details Herman's experiences as a prisoner in the Soviet Union during the 1930s and 1940s, including the harsh conditions he faced and the struggles he endured.

Herman was sent to the labor camp when he was just 18 years old for protesting the Soviet government's treatment of American citizens in Moscow. During his time in the camp, he worked in brutal conditions, endured extreme cold temperatures, and suffered from starvation and illness.

Despite the hardships he faced, Herman managed to survive and eventually escaped from the labor camp. He made a daring journey through Siberia and eventually made his way back to the United States.

"Coming Out of the Ice" was published in 1979 and was later adapted into a TV movie starring John Savage as Victor Herman. The memoir has been praised for its powerful depiction of Herman's experiences in the Soviet Union and his determination to survive against all odds.
